cards.question: Danish's old notice said only 'Dress decently'. What is its main weakness?
options: It is vague, so staff and supervisors read it differently and apply it unfairly
It is too long and detailed
It allows too many faith items
It sets strict safety rules
cards.explanation: A vague rule invites personal opinions about what is 'decent'. Clear examples and reasons help everyone apply the code the same way.

cards.title: Attire by risk and client contact
cards.caption: Place each role group, then set rules that fit its real needs.

items.label: Front desk and showroom
items.detail: High client contact, low risk: business casual or uniform, neat and consistent.

items.label: Client site visits
items.detail: High client contact, high risk: PPE plus a company jacket or neat workwear.

items.label: Back office
items.detail: Low client contact, low risk: business or smart casual, more flexibility.

items.label: Machine floor and workshop
items.detail: Low client contact, high risk: PPE and safe, fitted workwear first.

cards.back: Protects the head on sites with falling objects. It must fit properly; find solutions with workers who wear turbans or other head coverings.
Protect feet from heavy objects and sharp items. Usually required on sites and factory floors.
Makes people easy to see around vehicles and machines. Wear it over your normal clothes.
Protect hands from cuts, chemicals or heat. Use the right type for the task.
Protect eyes from dust, chips and splashes.
Protects hearing in loud areas such as print rooms and workshops.
Tuck in or pin dupattas, scarves and long hair, and remove dangling jewellery near moving parts.

cards.title: Safety comes first, and fits everyone
cards.body:
Where a role has real risks, safety clothing and PPE are not a matter of style. Managers should:

- **Identify the risks** in each area and decide what protection is needed.
- **Provide the PPE**, show people how to use it and replace it when worn.
- **Make it fit everyone**, including different body sizes, pregnant workers and people who wear turbans, hijabs or beards. Work with the person to find a safe option.
- **Apply it to everyone**, including managers and visitors.

Safety laws and rules differ between countries, provinces and industries. Follow the rules that apply to your workplace and get expert advice when you are unsure.

cards.title: The torn jeans conversation
cards.situation: A new worker in Danish's dispatch area has come in faded, torn jeans three days in a row. The new dress code asks for neat trousers or shalwar. A supervisor wants to tell him off in front of the team.

choices.text: Danish asks the supervisor to wait, then speaks to the worker privately, explains the code and why, asks if anything is making it hard, and offers a shop shirt and trousers from the uniform stock.
choices.outcome: The worker explains he has only one pair of trousers until his first salary. He is relieved, accepts the uniform and is grateful. Private, kind and practical works best.

choices.text: Danish sends the worker a short written warning without talking to him.
choices.outcome: The rule is clear, but the worker feels judged and the real reason, money, is not discovered. A conversation first would have solved it.

choices.text: The supervisor tells him off in front of the team.
choices.outcome: The worker is embarrassed, the team feels uneasy and trust drops. Public criticism of attire is never appropriate.

cards.title: A private, respectful attire conversation
cards.prompt: Put these steps of an attire feedback conversation in a good order.
steps: Check the facts and the exact policy wording first
Choose a private place and time; offer a same-gender colleague if the person prefers
Describe the specific item and the policy reason, not the person's body or character
Ask if anything makes it hard to follow, and listen
Agree a practical step, such as a uniform item or a date
Follow up kindly and treat the matter as closed once it is fixed

cards.title: Fair code or unfair code?
cards.prompt: Sort each dress code rule.

items.text: Closed shoes for everyone on the machine floor
Make-up compulsory for female front-desk staff only
Faith items such as hijab, turbans and kara are welcome
Managers may ignore the safety rules
Business casual with Western and local examples for all
Staff must buy the uniform themselves at full cost, with no notice
Medical needs may be met with adapted clothing

cards.question: During an attire feedback talk, which sentence keeps the focus on the policy, not the person?
options: 'You always look untidy and lazy.'
'Those clothes do not suit your body shape.'
'Everyone has been talking about how you dress.'
'Our code asks for neat trousers in dispatch, and these jeans are torn.'
cards.explanation: Good feedback names the specific item and the policy reason. Comments on character, body or gossip are hurtful and unprofessional.

cards.title: The manager's response
cards.prompt: Match each attire issue to a fair response.

pairs.left: A worker's dupatta end hangs near a moving machine
pairs.right: Ask her to pin or tuck it, and offer a safe way to wear it

pairs.left: A supervisor criticises a colleague's abaya
pairs.right: Remind the supervisor that faith dress is allowed and speak to them privately

pairs.left: A worker has only one set of work clothes
pairs.right: Offer uniform items and discuss support privately

pairs.left: A manager skips the hard hat on site
pairs.right: Apply the rule to the manager too, every time

pairs.left: Staff do not understand a new rule
pairs.right: Explain it again with examples and the reason behind it

cards.title: Danish's new one-page dress code
cards.body:
With Farah's help, Danish replaced 'Dress decently' with one clear page:

- **Why:** 'We dress to stay safe, to keep the shop clean and to represent Akhtar Printers well to customers.'
- **Machine floor:** shop shirt, trousers or shalwar, closed safety shoes, ear protection near the large printers, no loose items near machines. Dupattas and scarves pinned or tucked in.
- **Front counter:** neat business casual or shop shirt; Western or local wear both welcome.
- **Everyone:** clean, neat clothes; faith items welcome; talk to Danish about any health or faith need.
- **Support:** two shop shirts provided free to every worker.

He read it aloud in Urdu at a team meeting, invited questions and promised to review it in a year.

cards.title: Communicating a dress code well
cards.body:
- **Write simply** and give examples, with pictures where helpful.
- **Share it at joining**, not after a problem.
- **Translate** it into the languages your staff use.
- **Explain the reasons** in a short team meeting and invite questions.
- **Give notice** before changes, especially if staff must buy anything.
- **Model it:** managers follow the same code.
- Where there are legal requirements, such as safety rules, check the current rules with an expert.

cards.title: Take-aways from The Policy Room
items: Every dress code rule needs a reason: safety, hygiene, client contact or representing the organisation.
Write codes by outfit type, with Western and local examples, and the same standard for all genders.
Allow faith items and health needs, and find safe solutions together where PPE is needed.
Give attire feedback privately, about the policy, never about the body, and listen to reasons.
Provide PPE, train people and apply safety rules to everyone, managers included.
Share the code clearly at joining, translate it, model it and review it regularly.

cards.prompt: Imagine you lead a small team. Write three short rules for its dress code, each with a reason. Then check each rule: is it fair to all genders, faiths, health needs and budgets?

quiz.question: What should every rule in a dress code have?
options: A brand name to follow
A different version for each gender
A fine for every mistake
A clear reason, such as safety, hygiene or client contact
quiz.explanation: Rules with reasons are easier to follow and to apply fairly. If a rule has no reason, it may not be needed.

quiz.question: Where should a manager give feedback about an employee's attire?
options: In front of the team so others learn
In the company group chat
In private, with a calm and respectful tone
Through gossip with a supervisor
quiz.explanation: Attire feedback is personal. Private conversations protect dignity and make it easier to find a solution.

quiz.question: Which PPE item protects workers' hearing in a loud print room?
options: A high-visibility vest
Safety glasses
Ear protection, such as earplugs or earmuffs
A hard hat
quiz.explanation: Ear protection reduces noise reaching the ears. Vests, glasses and hats protect against other risks.

quiz.question: A worker's dupatta end hangs close to a moving machine. What is the fair, safe response?
options: Ask her to pin or tuck it in and offer a safe way to wear it
Ban dupattas everywhere in the company, so that no one ever has to think about the risk
Ignore it because dress is a personal choice
Shout at her in front of the team
quiz.explanation: Loose items near machines are a real hazard. Securing them keeps her safe while respecting her choice to wear a dupatta.

quiz.question: Which dress code rule is fair?
options: Business casual with Western and local examples, for all staff
Make-up compulsory for female staff only
Managers are exempt from safety shoes
Turbans and hijabs must be removed on client days
quiz.explanation: Fair rules apply equally, allow faith dress and include practical examples for everyone.

quiz.question: In an attire conversation, a worker says he has only one pair of trousers until his first salary. What is the best response?
options: Give him a written warning straight away so he understands that the rules are serious
Tell the team so they can donate clothes
Send him home without pay until he buys new clothes
Offer uniform items or support privately and agree a practical next step
quiz.explanation: Listening uncovers the real reason. Practical, private support solves the issue and keeps his dignity.

quiz.question: Danish's notice said only 'Dress decently'. Why did it cause problems?
options: It was too strict about safety and stopped people from wearing comfortable clothes at work
'Decently' was read differently by different people, so it was applied unfairly
It named too many examples
It was written in Urdu and English
quiz.explanation: A vague word lets personal opinions decide. Clear examples and reasons create consistency.

quiz.question: A role has high client contact and high safety risk, such as client site visits. Which attire approach fits?
options: A formal suit with no PPE so clients are impressed
PPE first, plus a company jacket or neat workwear
Any casual clothes because it is outdoors
PPE only for junior staff, not managers
quiz.explanation: Safety comes first, and neat company workwear represents the organisation. Rules apply to everyone on site.

quiz.question: Which sentence is the best way to open an attire feedback conversation?
options: 'People think you look careless, and I agree with them, so please sort it out by tomorrow.'
'Our code asks for closed shoes here, and today you have sandals. Can we talk?'
'Your clothes do not suit someone your size.'
'I am not saying anything, but others have noticed.'
quiz.explanation: Name the specific item and the policy, then invite a conversation. Avoid gossip, body comments and vague hints.

quiz.question: A worker who wears a turban needs head protection on site. What is the manager's best approach?
options: Find a safe option together under the rules that apply, without forcing removal
Remove him from site work permanently, so that the safety question never comes up again
Let him skip head protection with no further thought
Tell him to choose between his job and his faith
quiz.explanation: Managers should respect faith and safety together. Work with the worker and safety experts to find a suitable option under the rules that apply.

bank.question: A candidate is told the interview dress code is 'smart casual', but the role is client-facing. Which outfit is the wisest choice?
options: A neat polo shirt and chinos, exactly as stated
Gym clothes, because the code sounds relaxed
Business casual, one step above smart casual
A heavy embroidered wedding outfit to stand out
bank.explanation: For an interview, especially for a client-facing role, dressing one step above the stated code shows preparation and is easy to adjust.

bank.question: Which pair of reasons best explains why a bank asks counter staff to wear a uniform?
options: Fashion trends and staff entertainment
Saving electricity and reducing paperwork
Hiding staff from customers and managers
Representing the organisation and helping customers recognise staff
bank.explanation: Uniforms make staff easy to recognise and show a consistent image of the bank to customers.

bank.question: An office has no written dress code. Colleagues in similar roles wear pressed shirts, kurtas and plain shalwar kameez, and add blazers or waistcoats for clients. What is the unwritten code?
options: Casual, with no real expectations, because nothing is written down anywhere
Formal suits and ties every day
Uniform, because everyone looks similar
Business casual, stepping up to business formal for client meetings
bank.explanation: Reading what people in similar roles wear on normal days and client days tells you the real code.

bank.question: Which statement about attire and judgement is consistent with this course?
options: Outfits are judged against a setting, never people against a standard of looks
Attractive people should be given client roles because customers always prefer them
Expensive clothes show that a person is more capable
A person's body shape decides which dress code applies to them
bank.explanation: The course separates suitability of clothes for a setting from any judgement of bodies, faith or income.

bank.question: Maham's welcome email says 'dress appropriately' and her first day includes a meeting with a senior manager. Which plan is best?
options: Wear neat business casual, observe colleagues and ask her manager about the norm
Wear casual clothes on the first day and wait for someone to correct her if needed
Wear party clothes to make a strong impression
Ask a friend at another company what they wear and copy it
bank.explanation: A neat, slightly formal outfit is safe when unsure, and asking politely reveals the real expectations.

bank.question: A lab assistant asks why lab coats and closed shoes are required when the lab is not client-facing. What is the main answer?
options: They make the lab look more professional in adverts and photos for the company website
They are only for first impressions on visitors
They are a tradition with no practical purpose
They protect against spills, splashes and dropped items: the reason is safety
bank.explanation: In labs, protective clothing reduces harm from chemicals and accidents. Safety, not image, is the main reason.

bank.question: Which outfit sits at the formal end of the ladder of formality?
options: A printed lawn suit with sandals
A neat polo shirt with chinos
A plain, dark shalwar kameez with a formal waistcoat
A T-shirt with clean jeans
bank.explanation: A dark, plain shalwar kameez with a waistcoat is a formal look in Pakistan, comparable to a suit. The others are smart casual or casual.

bank.question: Omer can afford only one of these. Which gives his internship wardrobe the most value?
options: A trendy jacket in a colour that matches nothing he owns
A third pair of almost identical shoes
Tailoring his two existing trousers so they fit well
A large set of accessories he rarely wears
bank.explanation: Good fit makes existing clothes look much better. Spending on fit and versatile pieces gives the best value.

bank.question: Which fit problem is usually the hardest to fix with alterations?
options: Trouser hems that are too long
Sleeves that are slightly long
A loose button
Shoulders that are too wide or too narrow
bank.explanation: Hems, sleeves and buttons are simple fixes. Shoulders are built into the structure of a shirt or jacket and are hard to alter.

bank.question: Maham's wardrobe has black trousers, a grey shalwar, a white blouse and a navy kurta. Which item would add the fewest new outfits?
options: A plain cream kameez
A bright orange top that matches only one patterned dupatta
A navy cardigan
A light blue shirt
bank.explanation: Neutral pieces mix with many items. A colour that matches only one accessory adds very few combinations.

bank.question: Which ironing order is most sensible for a shirt or kameez?
options: Collar, cuffs and sleeves, shoulders and back, then front
Front, then collar, then hang it in a pile
Back only, because the front shows less
Sleeves last, after folding it into a drawer
bank.explanation: Starting with small parts such as the collar and cuffs, and finishing with the large front panels, avoids creasing finished areas. Hang it straight away.

bank.question: A winter client meeting is in Islamabad. Which choice is suitable and comfortable?
options: A thin lawn suit with no layers, because meeting rooms are usually heated in winter
A sports hoodie over formal trousers
A shiny party outfit with open sandals
A warm, dark shalwar kameez with a waistcoat, or a suit with a coat
bank.explanation: Warm, neat layers keep you comfortable and formal enough. Lawn suits summer; sports wear and party wear do not suit client meetings.

bank.question: Why do many advisers suggest letting leather shoes rest a day between wears?
options: Leather shoes are not allowed to be worn two days in a row under most office codes
It makes the shoes look newer immediately
It removes the need to clean them
It lets moisture dry out, which helps the leather last longer
bank.explanation: Shoes absorb sweat during the day. Rest, cleaning and polishing help them last.

bank.question: Which statement about local and Western business wear is accurate?
options: Only Western suits are professional in offices
Both are professional when neat and suited to the dress code
Local wear is only allowed on Fridays everywhere
Local wear must always be heavily embroidered
bank.explanation: A pressed shalwar kameez or kurta can be just as professional as a shirt and trousers, depending on the code and occasion.

bank.question: Which routine best prevents a stressful morning before an important meeting?
options: Deciding what to wear after breakfast
Ironing in the car on the way
Choosing, checking and ironing the outfit the night before
Wearing the same shirt as yesterday to save time
bank.explanation: Preparing the night before gives time to spot stains or loose buttons and keeps the morning calm.

bank.question: A colleague says beards look careless and should be banned in the office. Which response matches this course?
options: Beards should only be allowed for managers, so that junior staff keep a uniform look
Beards are fine only if they are dyed
He is right; only clean-shaven faces look professional
A clean, groomed beard is professional, and many people keep one for faith or choice
bank.explanation: Professional grooming is about cleanliness and neatness, not removing beards. Faith and personal choices deserve respect.

bank.question: Which habit has the highest impact for the lowest effort?
options: Keeping nails clean and breath fresh
A weekly visit to a salon for styling
Buying new shirts every month
Learning complex make-up techniques
bank.explanation: Clean hands and fresh breath are noticed in every handshake and conversation, and they take very little effort.

bank.question: Why does fragrance not replace washing?
options: It only covers smells for a while and does not remove sweat or bacteria
Fragrance is not allowed in any workplace, so washing is the only legal way to stay fresh
Fragrance makes clothes shrink
Fragrance only works on Fridays
bank.explanation: Washing removes the cause of body odour. Fragrance masks it briefly, and too much can bother colleagues.

bank.question: A woman colleague chooses not to wear make-up. A supervisor says she looks 'unprofessional'. What is the right view?
options: The supervisor is right, because make-up is required
Make-up is a personal choice; a clean, neat look is professional without it
She should wear make-up only on client days
Only men may choose not to wear make-up
bank.explanation: No one should be required to wear make-up. Requiring it for one gender only also makes a dress code unfair.

bank.question: Which item is least useful in a small grooming kit for a hot day?
options: Tissues or a small towel
A large bottle of strong perfume
A comb
A bottle of water
bank.explanation: Strong perfume can overwhelm others and does not refresh you. Tissues, a comb and water help you freshen up.

bank.question: Why should long hair be tied back in some jobs?
options: For safety near machines or hygiene around food
Because long hair is unprofessional in all offices
Because managers prefer one hairstyle
Because it is the latest trend
bank.explanation: Hair of any length is professional when neat. Tying it back is about safety or hygiene in specific roles.

bank.question: Maham is the main speaker at a client meeting where her team wears business casual. Which principle applies?
options: Speakers should dress more casually than the audience so they look friendly and relaxed
The speaker should wear the brightest outfit in the room
Dress does not matter if the slides are good
Speakers and hosts usually dress one step more formal than the audience
bank.explanation: Being at the front shows respect for the audience and supports confidence. One step up is usually right.

bank.question: Which video-call outfit is most likely to look good on camera?
options: A shirt with very fine, tight checks
A plain mid-tone kameez with simple earrings
A shiny metallic top under bright light
Several bangles that clink on the desk
bank.explanation: Plain mid-tone fabric shows well; fine patterns can flicker, shiny fabric reflects light and bangles can be loud on the microphone.

bank.question: On Friday, a corporate client will visit the shop. Omer is wearing a neat shalwar kameez. What is the best step?
options: Add a waistcoat and check that his clothes and shoes are clean and pressed
Change into gym clothes to look energetic
Leave his sleeves rolled up to look hardworking
Go home to change and miss preparing the samples
bank.explanation: A pressed shalwar kameez with a waistcoat is a smart, respectful look. He can step up without losing preparation time.

bank.question: Which statement about attending a colleague's wedding is most suitable?
options: Wear your office uniform to show loyalty to the company in front of your manager and colleagues
Wear the same outfit as the couple to show support
Wear festive attire that fits the invitation, while remembering colleagues and managers will see you
Dress as casually as possible because it is not work
bank.explanation: Weddings welcome festive clothes. Respect the invitation and the couple, and keep work relationships in mind.

bank.question: Before a first work trip abroad, which combination of checks is best?
options: Only the price of clothes at the destination, so you can buy everything there after you land
Host company guidance, official travel advice, the weather and the meeting schedule
A single social media post about the country
Nothing, because business dress is the same everywhere
bank.explanation: Norms, rules and weather differ. Reliable, current sources and your own schedule tell you what to pack.

bank.question: Which is the best reason to keep one meeting outfit in hand luggage?
options: Airlines charge less for hand luggage with clothes
It protects your key appointment if checked luggage is delayed
Clothes in hand luggage never crease
Security checks require it
bank.explanation: Delayed bags are common enough that a meeting outfit in hand luggage is a sensible safeguard.

bank.question: Maham will walk past printing machines during a talk at a print shop. Which outfit choice matters most?
options: High heels and a formal suit, because a guest speaker should look as formal as possible
A long flowing scarf for a festive look
Closed shoes and no loose dupatta ends or scarves near the machines
Clinking bangles to look elegant
bank.explanation: Even a short visit to a machine area needs safe attire. Closed shoes and secured fabric reduce the risk of accidents.

bank.question: A visitor asks a colleague to remove her hijab for a team photo 'so everyone looks the same'. What is the right response?
options: Explain politely that her hijab is her choice and stays on
Ask her to remove it just for the photo
Leave her out of the photo
Ask everyone to wear a scarf for fairness
bank.explanation: Faith-based dress is a personal choice and part of a person's identity. A team photo does not need everyone to look the same.

bank.question: Which compliment is the most appropriate at work?
options: 'You look slimmer this month.'
'You always come well prepared to client meetings.'
'You would look even better with fairer skin.'
'You are too pretty to be an engineer.'
bank.explanation: Compliments on effort and work are safe. Comments on bodies, skin colour or looks can hurt and reinforce bias.

bank.question: Which statement best explains 'modesty is personal, both ways'?
options: Only conservative dress is modest
Modesty rules apply only to women in offices
No one is forced to cover more, or to remove coverings, to fit in
Modesty is decided by the most senior manager
bank.explanation: Respect means accepting each person's choice in either direction, while keeping a shared standard of neatness.

bank.question: Which dress code clause fails the fairness test?
options: All staff wear closed shoes on the factory floor
Faith items such as kara and turbans are welcome
Female front-desk staff must wear heels; male staff have no matching rule
Adapted clothing is allowed for medical needs
bank.explanation: Rules that put extra cost or effort on one gender are unfair. A fair code asks the same of everyone.

bank.question: In a meeting, a colleague mocks Jaspal's turban. Which action from a teammate is most effective?
options: Laugh to reduce the tension, then change the subject quickly so nobody feels awkward
Calmly ask to keep it respectful, then support Jaspal
Tell Jaspal to ignore it because it was a joke
Say nothing now and gossip about it later
bank.explanation: Calm, visible support stops the behaviour, and a follow-up check-in and HR route help the person affected.

bank.question: After a careless comment about a colleague's dupatta, what is the best apology?
options: 'I am sorry if you were offended, but it was a joke.'
'Can you explain your culture so I understand why you are upset?'
'I am sorry, that was unkind. I will not say that again.'
'Everyone says it, so I did not think it mattered.'
bank.explanation: A short apology that owns the mistake and promises change is best. Excuses or asking the person to educate you add to the hurt.

bank.question: A global team includes partners in a hijab with a suit, a turban with a blazer and short-sleeved shirts. What does this show?
options: Only one global business uniform is professional
Faith-based dress is unsuitable for international work
Professional attire varies by culture; neat, suitable and respectful matters
Everyone should copy the client's clothes exactly
bank.explanation: Professional dress looks different across countries and faiths. Respect and neatness are the common standard.

bank.question: Which order of steps builds a fair dress code best?
options: Copy another company's code word for word, publish it straight away, then punish any mistakes
Ask the owner's preference, then post it without explanation
Write one word such as 'decently' and let supervisors decide
Map roles, set purpose, draft with options, check fairness, consult and share, then review
bank.explanation: A code built from real roles and purposes, tested for fairness and shared clearly, is easier to follow and defend.

bank.question: A supervisor wants to criticise a worker's torn jeans in front of the team 'as a lesson'. What should the manager do?
options: Stop the public criticism and speak to the worker privately about the policy
Allow it, because public criticism sets a clear example and saves time for everyone
Post a photo of the jeans in the staff chat
Ignore the issue and never mention the policy
bank.explanation: Attire feedback must be private and respectful. Public shaming harms dignity and trust.

bank.question: In a private attire conversation, why should the manager ask if anything makes the code hard to follow?
options: To find a reason to issue a formal warning and keep a written record against the worker
There may be reasons such as money, health or faith that change the right solution
To make the conversation last longer
To learn gossip about other staff
bank.explanation: Listening uncovers the real cause, such as having only one set of clothes, so the manager can offer practical support.

bank.question: Which role group needs PPE and safe fitted workwear first, with less focus on client image?
options: Machine floor and workshop staff
Front-desk reception staff
Back-office accounts staff
Staff working from home
bank.explanation: Low client contact with high safety risk means protection comes first. Image matters more in client-facing roles.

bank.question: A senior manager visits the site floor without a hard hat, saying 'I will only be a minute'. What is the right response?
options: Let it pass because managers set their own rules
Ask a junior worker to give the manager theirs
Apply the PPE rule to the manager too, every time
Remove the rule for short visits
bank.explanation: Safety rules protect everyone and must be applied consistently. Managers who follow them also model good behaviour.

bank.question: Which practice best helps staff understand a new dress code?
options: Posting it on the notice board without notice and fining anyone who gets it wrong at first
Explaining it in a team meeting with examples and reasons, in the languages staff use
Sharing it only with supervisors
Changing it every month without telling anyone
bank.explanation: Clear communication, with reasons and translation where needed, helps everyone follow the code willingly.

bank.question: A worker who wears a hijab must use safety equipment near printing machines. What is the fair approach?
options: Ban hijabs on the machine floor, because any head covering is a risk near moving parts
Let her skip all safety rules out of respect
Move her to a different job without asking
Agree a safe way to secure the hijab together, without asking her to remove it
bank.explanation: Respecting faith and keeping people safe go together. Discussing a secure, close-fitting option with the worker meets both needs.

bank.question: Which statement about safety rules and PPE is accurate?
options: Rules vary by place and industry; follow yours and seek expert advice
One rule applies in every country, so a single international checklist is always enough
Safety rules apply only to junior staff
PPE is optional if workers are careful
bank.explanation: PPE and safety requirements vary. Managers should check the current rules that apply and get expert help when unsure.
